cells.tense: You are here holding direction while the material presses in, and you know what you are doing.
cells.ask: Name the next concrete piece of what you are carrying, do only that piece today, and stop cleanly when it is done.
cells.core: You're the one holding the line. Something is pressing on you, and you're still moving toward the goal with your own weight behind it — quiet, private, not performing for anyone. That's not stubbornness. It's strength borrowing from what you've already built.\n\nThe way through is not to grip harder or to go it alone forever. It's to let what you've genuinely built show. What you've been carrying has taught you something other people can see and work with. Let one piece of it land as a fact, not a complaint, and let the direction stay yours while that strength does its ordinary work.
cells.sheetLine: You're still moving, and the moving is yours.
cells.verb: to hold a direction through material pressure using your own private resources
cells.place: at the point where energy is aimed at a destination and is meeting resistance

cells.tense: You are already braced against a material weight that cannot be written yet, feet set before it lands.
cells.ask: Ask one person for their half of something you are carrying alone, then wait for their answer before you lift it again.
cells.core: You're braced for a weight that hasn't arrived. The pressure you're holding against isn't here yet, but the bracing is doing most of the lifting. This works when it holds without forcing: it contains what's coming instead of crushing it into shape early, and it stays aimed at the goal while it does. You've stopped aiming and started preparing.\n\nHand back one piece that isn't yours alone, and wait. You're not conceding anything. You're finding out that the pressure you've been braced against was going to ask less of you than you feared. Holding steady without forcing keeps a direction longer than bracing against a future you can't see.
cells.sheetLine: The load isn't here yet, but you're already braced against it.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that has already closed behind you, holding a direction you no longer turn toward.
cells.ask: Say out loud what you carried and what it cost, to one person who can hear it without handing it back.
cells.core: You aren't moving toward anything right now. The energy that used to point somewhere has stopped, and you're staying put at a threshold that is already behind you. It isn't laziness. You stopped turning toward the goal, and that's simply where you stand.\n\nThe way back starts with being seen, not with effort. The strength you ran on is private, and private strength can go a long time without anyone confirming it was real. Let one person hear what you carried to get here, and let them take it as finished rather than asking you to pick it up again. Release isn't defeat. One clean ending, no self-blame, and the direction can come back on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You held the line, then stopped at a door already closed.

cells.tense: You are already persisting toward a goal right now, and you are talking about it as just how things are.
cells.ask: Say "this is mine" out loud about one goal you have been describing as if it were just happening to you.
cells.core: You're already carrying it. The strength that shows up in private is doing the work, push after push, when nobody is watching — and you've been describing the goal and the effort as if it were landing on you from outside. You're the one who kept it moving. You keep leaving that part out.\n\nWhat you're building is building because you kept showing up for it. Say one piece of it is yours, out loud, to one person. You don't have to become more capable than you already are. Let what you've been carrying be counted as something you did, so the next stretch finds the same hand it found last time.
cells.sheetLine: You kept it moving. Start saying so.

attempts.check: The record does not say that the person has a private history of material scarcity, only that in this seat and phase the capacity for private endurance is what is being tested. A reader could reasonably say the source of the load is not material pressure but ordinary schedule or mood, and I am reading the card too literally onto the seat. If the read is wrong, the ask still teaches something real: breaking a direction into one visible piece, giving a load back plainly, or letting a clean piece of visible structure release with thanks are useful even when the load is not material. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any hint that the card explains or traces where the pattern came from or has been before, which I have kept out.
